opening_message:
Ticket 1: Edward Fleming (employee ID E042) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E042.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Edward Fleming (E042) is a full-time Payroll Specialist requesting write access to Source Code. As a full-time employee, max is write (admin only if role owns the system; Payroll Specialist does not own Source Code). Requested write is within policy, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB check: Edward Fleming (E042) is a CONTRACTOR with BASIC security training (this conflicts with the earlier note listing full-time). Contractors max is read without advanced training; write requested is above max, so recommend read.
reason: HR records (authoritative for employment type) list Edward Fleming (E042) as a full-time Payroll Specialist. Full-time employees may have up to write; admin is not permitted since Payroll Specialist does not own Source Code (owned by Engineer). The requested write level is at or below the maximum, so write is granted. Note: the Security agent's conflicting contractor classification is not relied upon since HR is the authority on employment type; even so, write is within the full-time maximum.
